source_text: Ἵνα δὲ μή τινες ἀλογισταίνοντες εἰς ἀποτροπὴν τῶν δεδιδαγμένων ὑφ᾿ ἡμῶν εἴπωσι πρὸ ἐτῶν ἑκατὸν πεκτήκοντα γεγεννῆσθαι τὸν Χριστὸν λέγειν ἡμᾶς ἐπὶ Κυρηνίου, δεδιδαχέναι δὲ ἅ φαμεν διδάξαι αὐτὸν ὕστερον χρόνοις ἐπὶ Ποντίου Πιλάτου, καὶ ἐπικαλῶσιν ὡς ἀνευθύνων ὄντων τῶν προγεγενημένων πάντων ἀνθρώπων, φθάσαντες τὴν ἀπορίαν λυσόμεθα. Τὸν Χριστὸν πρωτότοκον τοῦ θεοῦ εἶναι ἐδιδάχθημεν καὶ προεμηνύσαμεν λόγον ὄντα, οἷ πᾶν γένος ἀνθρώπων μετέσχε. Καὶ οἱ μετὰ λόγου βιώσαντες Χριστιανοί εἰσι, κἂν ἄθεοι ἐνομίσθησαν, οἷον ἐν Ἕλλησι μὲν Σωκράτης καὶ Ἡράκλειτος καὶ οἱ ὅμοιοι αὐτοῖς, ἐν βαρβάροις δὲ Αβραὰμ καὶ Ἀνανίας καὶ Ἀζαρίας καὶ Μισαὴλ καὶ Ἡλίας καὶ ἄλλοι πολλοί, ὧν τὰς πράξεις ἢ τὰ ὀνόματα καταλέγειν μακρὸν εἶναι ἐπιστάμενοι τανῦν παραιτούμεθα. Ὥστε καὶ οἱ προγενόμενοι ἄνευ λόγου βιάσαντες ἄχρηστοι καὶ ἐχθροὶ τῷ Χριστῷ ἦσαν καὶ φονεῖς τῶν μετὰ λόγου βιούντων· οἱ δὲ μετὰ λόγου βιώσαντες καὶ βιοῦντες Χριστιανοὶ καὶ ἄφοβοι καὶ ἀτάραχοι ὑπάρχσυσι. Δι᾿ ἣν αἰτίαν διὰ δυνάμεως τοῦ λόγου κατὰ τὴν τοῦ πατρὸς πάντων καὶ δεσπότου θεοῖ βουλὴν διὰ παρθένου ἄνθρωπος ἀπεκυήθη καὶ Ἰησοῦς ἐπωνομάσθη, καὶ σταυρωθεὶς καὶ ἀποθανὼν ἀνέστη καὶ ἀνελήλυθεν εἰς οὐρανὸν, ἐκ τῶν διὰ τοσούτων εἰρημένων ὁ νουνεχὴς καταλαβεῖν δυνήσεται. Ἡμεῖς δέ, οὐκ ἀναγκαίου ὄντος τανῦν τοῖ περὶ τῆς ἀποδείξεως τούτου λόγου, ἐπὶ τὰς ἐπειγούσας ἀποδείξεις πρὸς τὸ παρὸν χωρήσομεν.
thought_title: The Word in the World Before Christ
pass_a_gloss: So that some people may not think irrationally and turn away from what we have taught, saying that we say Christ was born one hundred and fifty years ago under Cyrenius, but that He taught what we say He taught later, in the time of Pontius Pilate, and so they call us irresponsible because all people before Him were irresponsible, we will resolve this difficulty. We have been taught that Christ is the firstborn of God and that He is the Word, with whom every race of humans has shared. And those who have lived with the Word, even if they were considered atheists, are Christians, such as Socrates and Heraclitus among the Greeks, and Abraham, Ananias, Azarias, Misael, and Elijah among the barbarians, and many others, whose deeds or names we know it would be long to recount, so we refrain from doing so now. So, those who lived before Him without the Word were useless and enemies of Christ and killers of those who lived with the Word; but those who have lived and live with the Word are Christians, fearless, and undisturbed. For this reason, through the power of the Word, according to the plan of the Father of all, the Master God, a man was born of a virgin and was named Jesus, and was crucified and died and rose again and ascended into heaven, from what has been said through so many things, the intelligent person will be able to understand. But we, since it is not necessary now to deal with the proofs of this, will proceed to the urgent proofs at hand.

choices.why: The Greek term 'ἄθεοι' literally means 'without God', but in this context, it refers to those who were considered to be without God or irreligious.
The Greek term 'ἐχθροὶ' means 'enemies' or 'haters', and in this context, it refers to those who are opposed to Christ.
The Greek term 'ἀτάραχοι' means 'undisturbed' or 'untroubled', and in this context, it refers to those who are not troubled or disturbed.
The Greek term 'νουνεχὴς' means 'intelligent' or 'discerning', and in this context, it refers to someone who is able to understand.
The Greek term 'ἀναγκαίου' means 'necessary' or 'needed', and in this context, it refers to something that is required or needed.

pass_b_english: To keep some from reasoning irrationally and turning away from what we have taught, we will clear up the difficulty beforehand. They might claim that we say Christ was born a hundred and fifty years ago under Cyrenius, yet that He taught what we proclaim later, under Pontius Pilate, and so accuse us of being irresponsible because all people before Him were irresponsible. We have been taught that Christ is the firstborn of God and that He is the Word, with whom every race of humanity has shared. Those who have lived in accord with the Word are Christians, even if they were considered atheists — among the Greeks, Socrates and Heraclitus and others like them; among the barbarians, Abraham, Ananias, Azarias, Misael, Elijah, and many others, whose deeds or names we know it would be long to recount, so we refrain from doing so now. Therefore, those who lived before Him without the Word were useless and enemies of Christ and killers of those who lived with the Word; but those who have lived and live with the Word are Christians, fearless, and undisturbed. For this reason, through the power of the Word, according to the plan of the Father of all, the Master God, a man was born of a virgin and was named Jesus, and was crucified and died and rose again and ascended into heaven; from what has been said through so many things, the intelligent person will be able to understand. But we, since it is not necessary now to deal with the proofs of this, will proceed to the urgent proofs at hand.
